notes_list.title: Hunsdiecker Reaction
notes_list.basic_overview: Silver salts of carboxylic acids undergo oxidative decarboxylative halogenation to produce alkyl halides with one fewer carbon atom.
notes_list.extra_info_content:
General pattern: RCOOAg + Br2/light → RBr + CO2 + AgBr. The carbon skeleton loses the carboxyl carbon. This one-carbon shortening is a common examination clue.

MECHANISM & STEPWISE EXPLANATION
The silver carboxylate reacts with halogen to form an acyl hypohalite-type intermediate, which decarboxylates to an alkyl radical; halogen capture gives the alkyl halide.
